decisions.title: Read your observed dexterous prayer scroll
decisions.why: The scroll can unlock Rigour, a permanent ranged prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts already using Bowfa or a twisted bow. Keeping the scroll in storage provides no permanent unlock.
decisions.alternative: Keep using your currently available lower-level prayers and save the scroll if you deliberately want a spare. Another gear grind is not required to read this owned scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Reading consumes this scroll. The unlock remains after consumption; it does not prove that your levels already allow using the prayer.
decisions.effort: Small one-off action once the observed scroll is retrieved and unnoted. No drop grind or time estimate.
decisions.access: An observed scroll and confirmed locked prayer; no skill requirement to read. Retrieve from bank first if needed.
decisions.completion: Rigour unlock varbit is true; scroll absence is never completion evidence.
decisions.applicability: A positive inventory/equipment/session-bank observation of the exact scroll and a known false unlock.

decisions.title: Train Prayer to 74 for your unlocked Rigour
decisions.why: You already unlocked Rigour, a permanent ranged prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts already using Bowfa or a twisted bow. Prayer levels are the remaining confirmed gap to using it with your observed Defence level.
decisions.alternative: Use your currently available lower-level prayers and practise team CoX while building supplies. You do not need another dexterous scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Training uses bones and other supplies that could support different account goals. This is an optional preparation upgrade, not a raid entry requirement.
decisions.effort: Supply-dependent training; gathering and training method are outside this catalogue. No exact hours or RNG forecast.
decisions.access: Ordinary Prayer training; the catalogue applies only with confirmed unlock and 70+ Defence.
decisions.completion: Real Prayer level is at least 74.
decisions.applicability: Confirmed permanent unlock, known Prayer below 74, and known Defence at least 70.

decisions.title: Read your observed arcane prayer scroll
decisions.why: The scroll can unlock Augury, a permanent magic prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts with a high-end powered staff. Keeping the scroll in storage provides no permanent unlock.
decisions.alternative: Keep using your currently available lower-level prayers and save the scroll if you deliberately want a spare. Another gear grind is not required to read this owned scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Reading consumes this scroll. The unlock remains after consumption; it does not prove that your levels already allow using the prayer.
decisions.effort: Small one-off action once the observed scroll is retrieved and unnoted. No drop grind or time estimate.
decisions.access: An observed scroll and confirmed locked prayer; no skill requirement to read. Retrieve from bank first if needed.
decisions.completion: Augury unlock varbit is true; scroll absence is never completion evidence.
decisions.applicability: A positive inventory/equipment/session-bank observation of the exact scroll and a known false unlock.

decisions.title: Train Prayer to 77 for your unlocked Augury
decisions.why: You already unlocked Augury, a permanent magic prayer upgrade relevant to CoX, including accounts with a high-end powered staff. Prayer levels are the remaining confirmed gap to using it with your observed Defence level.
decisions.alternative: Use your currently available lower-level prayers and practise team CoX while building supplies. You do not need another arcane scroll.
decisions.tradeoff: Training uses bones and other supplies that could support different account goals. This is an optional preparation upgrade, not a raid entry requirement.

decisions.access: Ordinary Prayer training; the catalogue applies only with confirmed unlock and 70+ Defence.
decisions.completion: Real Prayer level is at least 77.
decisions.applicability: Confirmed permanent unlock, known Prayer below 77, and known Defence at least 70.

decisions.title: Plan ordinary team CoX with your observed weapons
decisions.why: You have recognised weapons across three styles and meet this catalogue's stated planning baseline. Agreeing a team setup with these options can be more useful than postponing practice for another weapon grind. This remains a repeatable prompt; raid history and player skill are unknown.
decisions.alternative: Use your observed rune crossbow if you decline CG; Bowfa with active crystal armour and a twisted bow are other recognised options. Dragon hunter crossbows, eclipse atlatl setups and dragon hunter wand spell setups appear in current CoX guidance but are outside this baseline. Review those with your team or a specialist planner; no mandatory Bowfa route is implied.
decisions.tradeoff: A learner team must agree your setup and supply roles. This catalogue does not establish raid access, armour completeness, weapon access unlocks, charges, ammunition, supplies or player skill. It does not certify solo or Challenge Mode readiness.
decisions.effort: Team coordination and practice; repeatable planning opportunity, not an inferred unfinished account unlock. Learning time varies.
decisions.access: Planning has no game requirement. CoX entry separately needs access to Great Kourend, which is unobserved. Equipping a lance additionally needs the Firemaking (not pyre), Fishing and Smithing sections of Barbarian Training; these unlocks are unobserved. Crystal equipment has quest requirements; this catalogue does not verify them.
decisions.completion: Repeatable planning prompt; no raid history is observed and no first-kill claim is made.
decisions.applicability: 80+ Attack/Strength/Ranged/Magic/Hitpoints and 70+ Defence/Prayer (authored preparation baseline, not game access); recognised positive weapons and their wield levels. Bowfa selection additionally needs observed active crystal pieces and 70 Agility.

decisions.title: Assemble a swamp trident from your observed magic fang
decisions.why: You have a magic fang and a seas trident. A swamp trident gives your CoX magic kit a stronger built-in spell without starting another weapon drop grind. This can still help a Bowfa account whose magic weapon remains a seas trident.
decisions.alternative: Keep using the seas trident if scale upkeep is unwelcome. An owned swamp trident, Sanguinesti staff, Eye of Ayak, Shadow or dragon hunter wand suppresses this assembly prompt; compare that option first. The wand needs a suitable spellbook, spells and runes, so possession alone does not establish a usable spell setup.
decisions.tradeoff: Uncharge the seas trident before assembly, retrieve and unnote components, then arrange runes and Zulrah scales. Using scales adds upkeep. A fang used here is unavailable for a toxic staff of the dead unless the trident is dismantled. No charges or supply quantities are inferred.
decisions.effort: Small assembly with owned parts; recurring scale and rune supplies vary with use. No drop-time estimate.
decisions.access: Assembly requires 59 Crafting, a chisel, magic fang and uncharged seas trident; enhanced seas tridents also work. Charging and wielding the result requires 78 Magic. Known real levels meet the thresholds; temporary boosts are not modelled.
decisions.completion: A recognised swamp trident (including uncharged/enhanced) or competing owned magic option ends this bounded assembly suggestion; this is not a claim that every alternative is best everywhere.
decisions.applicability: Positive fang, chisel and seas-trident observations; known Crafting 59+ and Magic 78+; completion must be confirmed false in supported storage. Unobserved containers keep completion unknown.

decisions.title: Compare your owned lance for the Olm melee role
decisions.why: You have a dragon hunter lance alongside a whip, tentacle or fang. Its dragonbane effect applies to Olm, so it is worth reviewing for that melee role even when your ranged kit is already established. This comparison does not call it the best weapon for every raid room.
decisions.alternative: Keep the whip or tentacle for a familiar setup, or retain the fang where its stab role suits your room plan. An observed scythe or Soulreaper axe suppresses this narrow comparison; use a specialist comparison for those weapons rather than assuming the lance wins.
decisions.tradeoff: Your equipped weapon is only the current loadout, not your usual CoX switch. Check whether you already bring the lance and agree room roles. The lance lacks the hasta's special attack; it does not replace a separate defence-reduction plan.
decisions.effort: Small kit review using owned gear; practice and inventory choices vary. No Hydra grind is suggested.
decisions.access: Comparing equipment has no game requirement. Wielding a lance requires 78 Attack plus the Firemaking (not pyre), Fishing and Smithing sections of Barbarian Training; the levels are checked, the miniquest sections are unknown. Actual raid access and other kit preparation remain unverified.
decisions.completion: Currently equipped lance or observed scythe/Soulreaper axe suppresses this comparison. This is a temporary loadout state, not permanent account completion.
decisions.applicability: Owned lance and a recognised ordinary melee alternative, Attack 78+, known equipment without lance, and no recognised competing melee weapon in observed storage.

decisions.title: Agree team defence-reduction coverage with your owned gear
decisions.why: You have recognised weapons across three styles and an owned defence-reduction weapon. Agreeing who brings which option is useful for established CoX teams as well as learners. Bowfa, a better staff or a lance does not establish the team's special-attack coverage.
decisions.alternative: A dragon warhammer, Bandos godsword and elder maul are current options with different drains and equipment costs. An owned elder maul avoids treating a warhammer as a mandatory new grind; BGS remains a complementary team option. If teammates cover the role, agree whether your inventory space is better used for supplies.
decisions.tradeoff: Defence reduction depends on the encounter and successful specials; these weapons are not interchangeable guarantees. Team loadouts and coverage are unknown. This is pre-raid planning, without live combat cues or certification of access, supplies or player skill.
decisions.effort: Small recurring team discussion using owned gear; no shaman, Bandos or raid-drop grind is required.
decisions.access: Planning has no game requirement. DWH wielding requires 60 Strength; BGS 75 Attack; elder maul 75 Attack and 75 Strength. The authored three-style planning baseline is preparation, not raid entry. Actual CoX access remains unverified.
decisions.completion: Repeatable team coordination; no team history or permanent completion is inferred.
decisions.applicability: The same recognised weapon and skill baseline as team planning, plus an observed reduction option and its wield levels. This more specific prompt shares the broad team-planning family.

decisions.title: Review an owned occult switch for your CoX mage kit
decisions.why: You have an occult necklace and a recognised charged magic weapon, while a fury is currently equipped. The occult supplies magic damage that the fury does not. Checking this switch can help an established Bowfa or staff account without another gear grind.
decisions.alternative: Keep the fury as a simpler hybrid switch if inventory space or switch complexity matters more. If you already bring the occult for mage, this review is already handled; current equipment cannot reveal your saved raid kit. An ornamented occult has the same combat stats.
decisions.tradeoff: A more specialised switch costs inventory space and attention; do not replace your melee/ranged necklace for all styles. The equipment observation is a prompt to review, not proof that you have forgotten your occult.
decisions.effort: Small owned-kit review with no Slayer grind or exact damage forecast; the benefit depends on the full loadout.
decisions.access: Wearing the occult requires 70 Magic. A recognised magic weapon and its wield level are checked. Owning an occult does not impose a Slayer requirement; acquiring it from smoke devils is outside this owned-kit comparison.
decisions.completion: Occult currently equipped suppresses this prompt; no usual raid setup or permanent loadout completion is inferred.
decisions.applicability: Positive occult observation, currently equipped normal/ornamented fury, Magic 70+, recognised charged magic weapon with its level. Empty or unknown equipment produces no suggestion.
